I saw my neighbours with their children and grandchildren the other day. They were so blissful together. I regret that I enstranged myself from my family and I wish I could go back in time to fix things.
</message>
output: You observe the harmony of others and feel the sting of your own isolation. Remember that the present moment is all you truly possess; the past is gone, and the future is uncertain. Consider what is within your power to amend today — perhaps a word, a gesture, or a change in conduct — and attend to that with care. Regret is a burden that weighs upon the mind; let it serve as a guide rather than a shackle.
